phrases.text: Just because you chose it years ago doesn't mean you're still choosing it now. Sometimes you're just moving inside the momentum of a decision you've already outgrown.
A pause is where you check if the commitment you're honoring is still in service to who you are now.

# The Lunar Nodes Enter Aquarius and Leo

Some transits ask for effort. The nodes ask for a direction. The dragon's head is the point of appetite, where the hunger arrives before the plan does. The dragon's tail is the point of release, where what is finished gets set down, willingly or otherwise. Together they are less a moment than an assignment, and the assignment just changed.

On {{entryDate}}, the North Node entered Aquarius and the South Node entered Leo, where they will work until {{exitDate}}. {{coEvents: same-day stations or ingresses, engine-confirmed, one sentence when present}} For the last year and a half the axis ran through Pisces and Virgo: surrender versus service, the checklist versus the mystery. That chapter is closing with its lessons finished or not. The new one runs through a different tension: standing out versus belonging.

Leo is about showing up, sharing your gifts, and letting yourself be seen. Aquarius is about the collective: working together, creating change that benefits everyone. With the North Node in Aquarius, the hunger points at the group: the community that needs rebuilding, the cause that could use your evening hours, the future that requires more than one person to build. Collectively, we get hungrier for systems that work, for belonging that is chosen rather than performed, for the rules we actually agreed to.

The South Node in Leo sets down the performance. Not the light itself: the applause-dependence. The version of you curated for the reaction. The leadership that cannot share a stage. The story where you are the main character of every situation, including other people's. The South Node does not take the skill away; it takes the hiding place. Leo's gifts stay: the warmth, the creative generosity, the courage to be seen. What gets released is being seen as the point.

The shadow work of this axis, named plainly: the times you shaped yourself to be accepted instead of showing up authentically, and the moments you withdrew just to prove you didn't need anyone. Both are the same wound wearing different costumes. Can you shine without making it all about you, and contribute to the group without disappearing? That question runs until {{exitDate}}, and it does not accept a one-word answer.

You don't have to disappear into the group to belong to it. You're allowed to be fully yourself in a crowd that didn't ask for a show. It may help to say this part out loud: "My people are waiting for exactly who I am."

## Eclipses on This Axis

Eclipses between {{entryDate}} and {{exitDate}} land in Aquarius or Leo, and they accelerate everything this chapter is teaching. Eclipses near the dragon's head open doors wherever Aquarius falls in your chart, often faster than you planned. Eclipses near the dragon's tail close doors wherever Leo falls, often more completely than you expected. The first eclipse on a new axis carries a particular charge: it introduces the chapter and announces its themes. This one arrives on {{firstEclipseDate}}.

A few eclipses in this window land in other signs, and those are the ones that confuse people. The Lunar Eclipse in Pisces on August 27, 2026 and the Lunar Eclipse in Virgo on February 20, 2027 still belong to the Pisces and Virgo story: the last chapter closing what it did not finish. When those arrive, expect an ending in that older territory, an unfinished surrender or a perfectionism finally retired, not a new assignment. The Lunar Eclipse in Capricorn on July 18, 2027 and the Lunar Eclipse in Cancer on January 11, 2028 are early previews of the axis that comes after this one, home and ambition, not homework due now. If a beginning or an ending near those dates feels bigger than its visible trigger, this is why.

One more amplifier, engine-confirmed as it forms: Pluto is already in Aquarius, and the North Node will cross it during this transit. When those meet, the collective questions about power, technology, and who the group serves get louder, and so do yours. {{plutoNodeAspect}}

## The Last Time

The nodes last ran through Aquarius and Leo from {{historyEntryDate}} to {{historyExitDate}}. The current passage will not repeat those events, but it returns to the same question at a new scale. If you were alive and remember those years, notice what began in your life then and what you finally put down. If you were alive but don't remember, your calendars, photos, and old messages from that window hold the pattern. If you weren't born yet, the world you inherited was partly shaped by what collectives built and what spotlights burned out in those years. If your family lived through it, you inherited some of their beliefs about belonging and visibility potentially without either of you discussing it directly. And if those years mean nothing to you personally, borrow them as evidence: another generation faced this same question about belonging and visibility, and what they built and what they let go of shows how much an answer can change a life.

This chapter runs until {{exitDate}}, the goal is never self-abandonment. The work is to find a place in a collective effort that does not cost you your name. By the time the nodes move on, your world won't look the same. Some shifts you will choose directly, and others will arrive to force your hand. Let them. Both are just clearing away the versions of your life you've already outgrown.

The North Node lands in your 11th house of friendships, groups, and the future, while the South Node settles into your 5th house of creativity, romance, and personal glory. The hunger grows toward community: the team that outlasts the season, the cause with your evening hours, the future built with people who don't need you to win.

I know: being the star is easier than being a member. But the dragon's tail is done funding the solo show: the romance treated as conquest, the project that only matters if your name goes first. You're allowed to matter in a group you don't lead. Your fire is still yours; it just gets a bigger fireplace.

The North Node enters your 10th house of career and public responsibility, while the South Node sinks into your 4th house of home, family, and the familiar script. The hunger grows toward the public role you keep deferring: the title, the visible responsibility, the work with your name on the door.

Staying home is comfortable, and comfort is your native language. But the tail is releasing the family's version of you: the role they cast you in before you could audition for anything else. You're allowed to outgrow the part your family wrote. The foundation stays; the ceiling goes.

{{transitThreads}} {{eclipseThreads}}

The hunger grows toward conviction: the long course, the philosophy tested by a journey, the work published under your name.

You can talk to anyone about anything, and that skill has been hiding you. The tail releases the endless gathering of options: the questions asked to avoid a decision, the wit that deflects the follow-up. You're allowed to conclude. An opinion held in public will teach you more this year than fifty conversations kept light.

{{transitThreads}} {{eclipseThreads}}

The hunger grows toward real merging: the joint plan, the debt faced together, the closeness that requires being witnessed rather than being the witness.

You provide so you never have to ask. But the tail is done with self-sufficiency as armor: the savings that substitute for trust, the comfort that keeps everyone at arm's length. You're allowed to need what you cannot provide yourself. That is not dependency; it is intimacy's entry fee.

{{transitThreads}} {{eclipseThreads}}

This axis lands closest to home for you, and it is not an insult. The hunger grows toward the equal partnership: the collaborator with a full vote, the relationship where the light is shared and nobody's dims.

Your instinct is to carry it all visibly and call that leadership. The tail releases the solo act: the identity that needs no one, the entrance that doubles as a wall. You're allowed to share the stage and still be the lead in your own life. The right partner does not reduce your story; they thicken the plot.

{{transitThreads}} {{eclipseThreads}}
